problems.title: Definition and calculation from the limit
problems.prompt: State the formal definition of the derivative at a point. Then, using only the difference quotient, calculate the derivative of \(f(x)=2x^2-x\).
steps: Definition: \(f^{\prime}(a)=\displaystyle\lim_{h\to0}\frac{f(a+h)-f(a)}{h}\), provided the limit exists and is finite.
We calculate the two values: \(f(a+h)=2(a+h)^2-(a+h)\) and \(f(a)=2a^2-a\).
We collect \(h\) to the numerator and we simplify, with \(h\neq0\): $$\frac{h(4a+2h-1)}{h}=4a+2h-1.$$
Passing to the limit \(h\to0\) we get \(f^{\prime}(a)=4a-1\), therefore \(f^{\prime}(x)=4x-1\).
problems.rubric: 2 pt correct definition · 3 pt quotient expansion · 1 pt limit and result

problems.title: Tangent and normal lines
problems.prompt: Given \(f(x)=x^3-3x\) and the point \(P=(2,2)\), find the equations of the tangent and normal lines to the graph at P.
steps: Let's go. \(f^{\prime}(x)=3x^2-3\). The point \(x=2\), slope of the tangent \(m_t=f^{\prime}(2)=12-3=9\).
We use the dot form–slope: \(y-2=9(x-2)\). Developing you get \(y=9x-16\).
The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, therefore his slope is the reciprocal change of sign: \(m_n=-1/9\).
Again with the dot form–slope: \(y-2=-\frac19(x-2)\)I mean, \(y=-\frac19x+\frac{20}{9}\).
problems.rubric: 2 p derivative and slope · 2 pt tangent · 2 pt normal

problems.title: Differentiation rules
problems.prompt: Calculate the derivatives and show the rule used: a) \(x^2e^x\); b) \((x^2+1)/(x-1)\); c) \(\sin(3x^2)\); d) \(\ln(1+x^2)\).
steps: c) Rule of composite function: derivative external is \(\cos(3x^2)\), the inner one is \(6x\). Therefore \((\sin(3x^2))^{\prime}=6x\cos(3x^2)\).
d) More composite function: \((\ln u)^{\prime}=u^{\prime}/u\), with \(u=1+x^2\). Therefore \((\ln(1+x^2))^{\prime}=\frac{2x}{1+x^2}\).
problems.rubric: 2.5 pt for each derivative: indicated rule, steps and result

problems.title: Second derivative and concavity
problems.prompt: For \(f(x)=xe^x\): a) calculate \(f′(x)\) and \(f′′(x)\); b) find and classify the stationary point; c) determine where concavity changes and locate the inflection point.
steps: With the product rule: \(f^{\prime}(x)=e^x+xe^x=e^x(x+1)\). Differentiatendo again: \(f^{\prime\prime}(x)=e^x(x+1)+e^x=e^x(x+2)\).
I stationary points meet \(e^x(x+1)=0\). For \(e^x>0\), must be \(x=-1\); the point is \((-1,-e^{-1})\).
Classification: \(f^{\prime\prime}(-1)=e^{-1}>0\), therefore the stationary point is a minimum local.
For \(e^x>0\), the sign of \(f^{\prime\prime}(x)=e^x(x+2)\) depends on \(x+2\): is negative for \(x<-2\) and positive for \(x>-2\).
Concavity changes in \(x=-2\), therefore The inflection point is \((-2,-2e^{-2})\).
problems.result: \(\boxed{f^{\prime}=e^x(x+1),\ f^{\prime\prime}=e^x(x+2)}\), minimum in \((-1,-e^{-1})\), inflection point in \((-2,-2e^{-2})\)
problems.rubric: 2 p derivatives · 3 p stationary point and classification · 3 pt sign f′′ and inflection point
